bull.b: The long-term Anthropic lease materially improves revenue visibility and validates TeraWulf’s ability to secure large-scale HPC customers. Contracted demand can support infrastructure utilization, recurring lease revenue, and a more durable business mix beyond bitcoin mining volatility.

Rapid growth in HPC leasing shows the company is converting data-center capacity into a higher-value revenue stream. A rising contribution from contracted leases could improve business durability, diversify earnings, and provide a foundation for scaling infrastructure over the next several quarters.

Greater committed borrowing capacity and a larger accordion give TeraWulf more flexibility to fund construction, letters of credit, and operating needs. This strengthens near-term execution capacity and supports expansion, although the company remains dependent on disciplined capital deployment.

bear.b: Gross profit has not translated into sustainable earnings because operating costs and non-operating charges remain exceptionally high. Persistent, deep losses can consume capital, weaken financial resilience, and make future expansion increasingly dependent on external financing or asset monetization.

Negative operating cash flow shows the core business is not currently self-funding, while substantial free-cash-flow deficits reflect heavy investment and ongoing cash demands. Continued burn raises funding, dilution, and execution risk as the company builds additional capacity.

Scaling multiple large data-center projects requires scarce electrical labor and coordination across changing customer designs. Persistent workforce and design constraints could delay capacity delivery, defer contracted revenue, and increase project costs before the planned infrastructure reaches full utilization.
